question:

(F) Cone

answer:
In spherical coordinates \((\rho, \theta, \phi)\), the angle \(\theta\) represents the azimuthal angle in the \(xy\)-plane from the positive \(x\)-axis. Fixing \(\theta = c\) means that all points with this \(\theta\) value will lie in a plane that makes an angle \(c\) with the positive \(x\)-axis. 

This plane extends infinitely in the \(z\)-direction, as \(\rho\) (the radial distance from the origin) and \(\phi\) (the polar angle from the positive \(z\)-axis) can vary freely. In Cartesian coordinates, this corresponds to the plane \(y = x \tan(c)\), which is indeed a vertical plane containing the \(z\)-axis.

Thus, the shape described by the equation \(\theta = c\) in spherical coordinates is a plane.

\(\boxed{C}\)
